facts.statement: Silutitan is a genus of euhelopodid sauropod dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous of Xinjiang, China.
facts.quote: Silutitan (meaning "Silk Road giant") is a genus of euhelopodid sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Shengjinkou Formation of Xinjiang, China.

facts.statement: The genus Silutitan contains only one species, Silutitan sinensis.
facts.quote: It contains only the type species, Silutitan sinensis.

facts.statement: A fossil site known as a Konservat-Lagerstätte was reported in the Hami region of Xinjiang, China, in 2006.
facts.quote: In 2006, a Konservat-Lagerstätte was reported from the Shengjinkou Formation in the Hami region of Xinjiang, China.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen IVPP V27874 was established for the new sauropod taxon Silutitan in 2021.
facts.quote: In 2021, these were established as the holotype (IVPP V27874) of the new sauropod taxon, Silutitan.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of six cervical vertebrae that all retain their neural spines.
facts.quote: Among the excavated fossils were six cervical vertebrae with all neural spines intact.

facts.statement: The genus name Silutitan refers to the Silk Road, and the species name sinensis refers to China.
facts.quote: The generic name, refers to the Silk Road (Silu in Mandarin), while the specific name, sinensis, refers to China.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Silutitan as the sister taxon to Euhelopus.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic analysis of Wang et al. places Silutitan as the sister taxon to Euhelopus

facts.statement: Silutitan belongs to the family Euhelopodidae.
Silutitan lived during the Valanginian stage of the Early Cretaceous, between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Valanginian (137.05 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: The fossil locality of Silutitan also contained the titanosaur Hamititan and the pterosaur Hamipterus.
facts.quote: Other animals from the holotype locality include the contemporary titanosaur Hamititan, which was described in the same paper, and the pterosaur Hamipterus.
